vopros: Who is behind Business Intelligence DNA (businessinteldna.com), and is it a legitimate company?

vyzhimka.tekst:
I looked into the website, its legal pages, domain history, and the Wyoming address it gives. My assessment: Business Intelligence DNA appears to be a very new, real operating business, but it has essentially no independent track record yet. I would distinguish “legally organized / identifiable” from “established and independently validated.”

The people behind it identify themselves as Andrii Zhyla and Maryna (“Masha”) Zhyla. The site's terms say that they personally perform the diagnostic/strategy work: Andrii handles strategy and positioning, while Maryna handles business economics and is described as a former CFO. Its privacy policy explicitly says there are only two people and no employees. ([businessinteldna.com](https://businessinteldna.com/terms))

The legal entity is given as Wealthboosterpro LLC, doing business as “Business Intelligence DNA,” a Wyoming LLC. The website gives the address 5830 E 2nd St, Suite 7000, Casper, WY 82609. ([businessinteldna.com](https://businessinteldna.com/contacts))

There is one important caveat concerning that address: it is not evidence that Andrii and Maryna operate a physical office there. The same address is used by many unrelated Wyoming LLCs and is associated with registered-agent/company-formation services. For example, Wyoming corporate filings for an unrelated company identify Republic Registered Agent LLC at exactly 5830 E 2nd St Ste 7000. ([dms.psc.sc.gov](https://dms.psc.sc.gov/Attachments/Matter/3e51ca5b-8ff8-4be3-b906-f7fee2aaf1f3?utm_source=openai)) So I would treat this as a registered/virtual corporate address rather than Business Intelligence DNA's actual place of operation.

The biggest reason for caution is how new the operation appears to be. The domain businessinteldna.com appears on a list of .com domains newly registered on September 6, 2026. ([com.all-url.info](https://com.all-url.info/21/25/?utm_source=openai)) The site's contact page is dated September 7, its original terms took effect September 8, and the current terms took effect September 14, 2026. Today is September 17, 2026. In other words, the public-facing business appears to be roughly 11 days old. ([businessinteldna.com](https://businessinteldna.com/terms))

I didn't find an established independent web footprint for “Business Intelligence DNA” or meaningful third-party customer reviews in the searches I ran. Searches for Wealthboosterpro LLC were also very thin. That isn't proof of anything improper, especially for a business that apparently just launched, but it means there isn't much outside evidence yet with which to verify its claims or performance.

There are some positive legitimacy signals. The site does substantially more disclosure than a typical throwaway/scam site: it names the underlying LLC and the two operators; publishes detailed terms, privacy documentation and an NDA; gives specific prices and refund/process-guarantee provisions; identifies Stripe as its payment processor; and spells out its data processors (including Anthropic, Google, ElevenLabs, Twilio, Stripe, etc.). ([businessinteldna.com](https://businessinteldna.com/terms)) The terms also explicitly say it does not guarantee business results. ([businessinteldna.com](https://businessinteldna.com/terms))

My conclusion would therefore be:

- “Is there a real identifiable business behind the site?” — Probably yes. The site identifies Wealthboosterpro LLC and Andrii and Maryna Zhyla rather than hiding behind an anonymous website.
- “Is this an established company with a demonstrated reputation?” — No evidence of that yet. The Business Intelligence DNA brand/domain appears to have launched in September 2026.
- “Does the Wyoming address establish a substantial U.S. office?” — No. It appears to be a registered-agent/virtual address used by numerous companies.
- “Would I call it a scam?” — I found insufficient evidence to justify that characterization.
- “Would I send them $5,000+ based solely on what is currently online?” — I would do additional due diligence first. Their own terms advertise implementation starting at $5,000, so the lack of an independent track record becomes material at that price point. ([businessinteldna.com](https://businessinteldna.com/terms))

One thing worth investigating further is Andrii and Maryna Zhyla themselves: their prior businesses/employment, whether Maryna's former-CFO background is independently verifiable, when Wealthboosterpro LLC was actually formed, who its registered members/managers are where publicly available, and whether either has litigation, regulatory, or business-history records. That would give a much stronger answer than evaluating an 11-day-old website alone.
